title: The Militarist
strengths: +2 Military Standing at start | Wins all combat ties | Declares Open War at no Grievance cost | Pays 1 less for War deck access
weaknesses: -1 Capital Standing at start | Cannot send Instigators | Spying always fails | Pays 2 Capital more for every Promise it proposes
signature: Call the Banners | Martial Law | Crush the Rebellion | The Iron Summons | No Quarter

title: The Spymaster
strengths: +2 Capital Standing at start | Draws 2 from its own House deck each turn | Sends 2 Instigators per turn | Spying always succeeds and is never detected
weaknesses: -1 Military Standing at start | Combat cards cost double | Pays 4 Grievance to declare Open War | Broken Words count double against it when cards read reputation
signature: Whisper Network | Poison | Blackmail | Double Agent | The Long Knife

title: The Banker
strengths: +5 Gold Standing at start | +2 Gold Levy every turn beyond Standing | Buys votes at Council for 2 Gold Levy each | Clears Unrest at 1 Gold per point | The Purchased Throne is a road only it can realistically walk
weaknesses: -1 Military Standing at start | Its lords cost 2 Levy of dues to maintain, not 1 | Revolution in its lords advances at double rate from Instigators | Buys votes and so buys the Paramountcy, and is resented for it in Grievance
signature: Bribe | Mercenaries | Buy the Vote | Debt Trap | Golden Shackles

title: The Legitimist
strengths: +2 Standing in all three at start | Each of its lords casts one extra vote at every Council | Revolution in its lords begins at -1, taken once when the Bond is sworn | May pardon a turning lord, ending its Revolution and gaining 2 Servitude over it
weaknesses: Cannot send Instigators against an unbound lord | Cannot assassinate | No permanent growth cards in its own deck | Loses 2 Capital Standing the first time it breaks a Promise each game
signature: Pardon | Call the Council | Oath Sworn | Defend the Realm | The People's Choice

title: The Word
words: A Lion's Word is a Lion's Claw
strengths: +2 Capital Standing at start | A kept Promise pays 1 Capital Standing outright -- the only routine way any House grows Standing | Its deck is mostly Promises, with every term in it
weaknesses: Breaking a Promise costs double Favour with the Court | No combat identity at all: it fights at the base of 3

title: The Yoke
strengths: Advances Servitude one notch deeper than anyone else | Revolution advances at half rate against lords it holds | +1 Military and +1 Gold Standing at start
weaknesses: Cannot spy: it binds in the open and has no use for whispers | -1 Capital, so the Council is harder to reach by any road but the lords

title: The Grudge
strengths: Every Grievance it gains, it gains one harder | The five Grievance sinks become a real economy rather than a floor | +1 Military and +1 Capital Standing at start
weaknesses: -1 Gold: it cannot buy its way anywhere | Its whole economy is being wronged, so a rival that leaves it alone starves it

title: The Beast
strengths: Unrest cuts its Levy at half rate: a realm in uproar is the one it rules best | +2 Military Standing at start
weaknesses: Cannot buy Favour -- it has nothing the Court wants | -1 Capital Standing at start
